Chapter 10: Integrating “Should” and “Must”: Living Authentically in a Complex World.
As we keep moving forward, something becomes pretty clear—“Should” and “Must” aren’t enemies at all. They’re actually two sides of the same coin, each with their own purpose. The real challenge? It’s not about getting rid of “Should” or living only by “Must.” Instead, it’s about discovering a balance that feels honest, doable, and really alive.
Think about a parent for a moment. They might feel a deep pull toward their creative work—that’s their “Must.” But at the same time, there’s the reality of looking after a family—their “Should.” That tension? It’s real. But it doesn’t have to lead to guilt or frustration. In fact, it can be an invitation—a chance to bring both parts together and honor them equally.
A lot of us picture authenticity as tossing out all our obligations. But honestly, it’s much more nuanced than that. Living authentically means making conscious choices. It’s about aligning what you do with what you truly value, and finding meaning in both “Should” and “Must.” Some “Shoulds” aren’t just necessary—they’re actually valuable. And “Must” doesn’t have to stay separate; it can become part of your everyday life.
Here’s a great example: one person realized they could bring their love for music into their teaching job. Suddenly, the lines between “Should” and “Must” weren’t so rigid anymore—they started to blend together. The result? Life felt more integrated, more whole.
And this isn’t a one-and-done kind of thing. The process keeps going. New challenges, new choices, new chances to adjust are always around the corner. What matters most is staying awake to what’s happening, listening closely to yourself, and choosing what feels true every time. Over time, “Should” and “Must” stop clashing—and start working in harmony.
